corrections.value: Entry to the park is generally open, but specific activities like backcountry camping require permits from the Visitor Centre in Fort Smith. Pine Lake Campground offers both reservable sites (via the Parks Canada Reservation System) and first-come, first-served sites.
corrections.quote: The Pine Lake Campground has both reservable and first come, first served campsites.
corrections.reason: Updated to reflect the availability of reservable sites which was previously omitted.

corrections.value: This trail is currently closed due to a collapsed sinkhole. Check at the Visitor Centre for status on the new route development.
corrections.quote: Karstland Trail: This trail is closed due to a collapsed sinkhole. We’re working on a new route.
corrections.reason: The trail is physically closed as of the audit date.

corrections.value: NOTE: Trail currently CLOSED. Previously a trek through jack pine forest to reach a secluded chain of lakes known for birdwatching and bison sightings. Check for wildfire rehabilitation updates.
corrections.quote: Lane Lake Trail | Closed. | 2026-07-06: Respect all posted notices and signs;
corrections.reason: Trail closed due to 2023 wildfire hazards.

corrections.value: Outside of the Fort Smith townsite, cellular service is extremely limited, though a public internet link exists on NWT Highway 5. It is still recommended to carry a satellite communication device for remote areas.
corrections.quote: Parks Canada and GNWT establish public Internet link on NWT Highway 5
corrections.reason: Corrects the claim of 'Total Connectivity Loss' given the new internet link.

summary: Wood Buffalo National Park is verified as Canada's largest, but the plan requires significant updates due to 2023 wildfire impacts which have closed the Lane Lake Trail and Karstland Trail (the latter specifically due to sinkhole collapse). Camping at Pine Lake is now partially reservable, and a public internet link has been established on Highway 5, contradicting the 'total connectivity loss' warning.
